name: Sawn vein-cut (across the bed)
process: The block is sawn into slabs with the saw plane across the bedding planes, so the face shows the edges of the layers. Slabs come from a gang saw (steel shot, chat or sand in a slurry, or diamond blades), a diamond wire or a disc; the sawn face is then left as sawn, or honed or polished.

creamMarble.text: Crema Marfil's veins belong to several families of stylolites and calcite veins.
creamMarble.source: Lopez-Buendia A.M., Guillem C., Cuevas J.M., Mateos F., Montoto M. (2013) 'Natural stone reinforcement of discontinuities with resin for industrial processing', Engineering Geology 166:39-51, abstract, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enggeo.2013.09.004

creamMarble.text: Botticino's stylolites run almost parallel to the sedimentation level, so a cut across the bed shows them as lines.
creamMarble.source: Cooperativa Cavatori Botticino, 'The Marble' (description and technical data to UNI EN test standards), read 2026-09-26, https://www.cavatoribotticino.it/en/the-marble/

photograph: Bands of ivory, cream and honey run the length of the slab, wavy, sometimes pinching out.
Voids are drawn out along the bands like small lenses and are smaller and more regular than in a cross-cut slab.
Each slab is a different slice of the same bed: tone and band character carry across a joint, the lines do not.
As sawn, a diamond gang saw leaves fine parallel markings.

unverified.reason: No measured band spacing for vein-cut Roman travertine was found.
